expertInsight: Pardot is now officially Marketing Cloud Account Engagement (MCAE) — Salesforce made the rename in 2022. The exam code (CRT-302) and 'Pardot Consultant' title haven't changed, so that's still what you'll search for and what shows up on your credential. Just don't be thrown when every screenshot in Trailhead or the product itself says Account Engagement instead of Pardot.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Account Engagement Consultant Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The Account Engagement Consultant exam is challenging. It tests strategic solution design for B2B marketing automation, including lead scoring and grading models, Engagement Studio program architecture, Salesforce sync configuration, and campaign attribution. Hands-on implementation experience is essential.
bullets: 68% passing score — slightly higher than some consultant exams, reflecting the depth of B2B marketing automation knowledge required.
Solution design focus — expect scenario questions asking you to design scoring models, multi-path Engagement Studio programs, and Salesforce sync architectures for specific business requirements.
CRM alignment tested — you must understand Pardot-Salesforce campaign alignment, the connector user's permissions, and how B2B Marketing Analytics extends attribution reporting.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Complete at least two full Pardot implementations covering scoring, Engagement Studio, and Salesforce sync before booking. Score 80%+ on practice exams to account for the higher passing threshold.

examFormat.heading: Account Engagement Consultant Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or in-person. Here is the format:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: About 55-65% of questions are scenario-based. You'll be given a B2B marketing requirement and asked to design a scoring model, recommend an Engagement Studio program structure, or configure the Salesforce sync architecture.
bestWayToPass: Master scoring and grading design: Know how to configure scoring categories, custom scoring rules, and grading profiles that align with a client's sales qualification criteria.
Design Engagement Studio programs: Practice building multi-branch nurture programs with conditional logic, re-engagement paths, and entry/exit criteria for complex B2B scenarios.

Understand Salesforce sync deeply: Know the connector user's required permissions, field sync behavior settings (Pardot wins, Salesforce wins, Most Recently Updated), and how to troubleshoot sync errors.
Study campaign attribution: Know the difference between Pardot first-touch campaigns and Salesforce multi-touch campaigns, and how Connected Campaigns and B2B Marketing Analytics extend reporting.

keyConcepts.h2: Pardot Consultant: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Implementation and Configuration
blocks.body: The [Pardot Consultant](/certifications/pardot-consultant) exam focuses on strategic configuration beyond the Specialist level. Implementation includes Business Unit setup, connector configuration (Pardot-Salesforce sync settings), user management across roles (Admin, Marketing, Sales), and account-level settings. The consultant designs the overall marketing automation architecture — single vs multi-business unit strategy, campaign attribution model, and integration with Salesforce CRM campaigns. Know the difference between Pardot Admin permissions and Salesforce Connected User permissions.

blocks.heading: Advanced Lead Nurturing Strategy
blocks.body: Consultant-level Engagement Studio design covers multi-path programmes, re-engagement campaigns, and cross-business-unit nurturing. Advanced scenarios include pause/resume logic, entry source management (lists, segments, dynamic entry), and Engagement Studio reporting (completions, active, stopped). The consultant selects between Engagement Studio, Automation Rules, and Segmentation Rules for complex nurturing requirements. Know when Salesforce Flow (triggered from Pardot via the connector) is more appropriate than Pardot-native automation.

blocks.heading: Pardot-Salesforce Campaign Alignment
blocks.body: Pardot Campaigns track first-touch attribution. Salesforce Campaigns track multi-touch attribution and enable influence reporting. Pardot Campaign Influence connects Pardot prospect activity to Salesforce Opportunities — configured via Campaign Influence settings. B2B Marketing Analytics (built on [CRM Analytics](/certifications/crm-analytics-einstein-discovery-consultant)) provides advanced attribution dashboards. The consultant designs the campaign data model — Campaign Hierarchy, campaign member statuses, and attribution window settings — to align marketing and sales reporting.

blocks.heading: Advanced Scoring, Grading, and Segmentation
blocks.body: Scoring Categories maintain separate score totals per product or business unit. Custom scoring rules allow point adjustments for specific activities beyond defaults. Profile criteria drive grading — the consultant designs the grade thresholds (A through F) and profile attributes that match the ideal customer profile. Segmentation Rules create static lists from criteria at a point in time (unlike Dynamic Lists which are ongoing). The consultant architects the scoring and grading model to align with sales qualification criteria.

blocks.heading: Reporting, ROI, and B2B Marketing Analytics
blocks.body: The Pipeline Report connects Pardot activities to Salesforce Opportunities — showing which campaigns generated pipeline. Engagement History embedded on Salesforce records shows individual prospect activity timelines. B2B Marketing Analytics (**Einstein Analytics** for B2B) provides pre-built dashboards for engagement, pipeline influence, and campaign performance. The consultant designs the reporting strategy to demonstrate marketing ROI to leadership and aligns metrics to business outcomes (MQL-to-SQL rate, campaign attribution, pipeline influence %).

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Marketing Cloud Account Engagement Consultant Exam
scenarioTips.intro: The Account Engagement (Pardot) Consultant exam tests solution design for B2B marketing automation. Scenarios ask you to design nurture programs, lead scoring models, and Salesforce sync configurations for specific business requirements.

blocks.heading: Lead Scoring & Grading Design
blocks.body: Scoring measures prospect engagement (activity-based); Grading measures fit (demographic-based). Know how to configure scoring categories, custom scoring rules, and grading profiles to align sales and marketing on lead quality.

blocks.heading: Engagement Studio (Nurture Programs)
blocks.body: Know all Engagement Studio trigger, rule, and action types. Understand how to design multi-branch programs, set wait times, and use rules to route prospects based on behavior or CRM data.

blocks.heading: Salesforce Sync Architecture
blocks.body: Understand the sync between Pardot (Prospects) and Salesforce (Leads/Contacts), sync triggers (Salesforce Connector user, **assignment rules**), and how to troubleshoot sync errors. Know the connector user's required permissions.

blocks.heading: Forms, Landing Pages & Tracking
blocks.body: Know how to configure Pardot forms vs. form handlers (for external forms), landing page redirects, custom redirects for tracking links, and how the Pardot tracking pixel works across sites.

blocks.heading: Campaign Reporting & Attribution
blocks.body: Understand Pardot campaign metrics, the Engagement History component, and how B2B Marketing Analytics extends reporting. Know the difference between first-touch and multi-touch attribution models.

sampleQuestions.question: A client wants to implement lead scoring that accounts for both explicit and implicit data. What should the consultant recommend?
options: Use both Scoring and Grading together
sampleQuestions.explanation: Using both Scoring (implicit data/behavior) and Grading (explicit data/profile fit) together provides a complete picture of lead quality.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the recommended approach for syncing Pardot prospects to Salesforce Leads vs Contacts?
options: Use connector settings to define sync behavior
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Salesforce connector settings allow you to configure whether prospects sync to Leads or Contacts based on matching rules and business requirements.

sampleQuestions.question: A company has multiple business units. How should Pardot be configured?
options: Multiple Business Units with separate prospect databases
sampleQuestions.explanation: Multiple Business Units allow separate prospect databases, user permissions, and branding while sharing a single Salesforce org.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the best practice for implementing progressive profiling?
options: Use progressive profiling feature in form settings
sampleQuestions.explanation: Pardot's progressive profiling feature automatically shows different fields to returning visitors based on what data you already have.

sampleQuestions.question: How should connected campaigns be used?
options: To sync Pardot and Salesforce campaigns bidirectionally
sampleQuestions.explanation: Connected Campaigns allows bidirectional sync between Pardot and Salesforce campaigns, enabling unified reporting and ROI tracking.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of Engagement Studio programs?
options: To automate multi-step email and action programs based on prospect behavior
sampleQuestions.explanation: Engagement Studio automates nurture and behavior-based programs.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Pardot feature supports A/B testing for landing pages?
options: Landing page A/B testing with variants
sampleQuestions.explanation: Landing pages support A/B testing with multiple variants.

sampleQuestions.question: How should automation rules differ from Engagement Studio?
options: Automation rules are if-then; Engagement Studio is multi-step programs
sampleQuestions.explanation: Automation rules are if-then; Engagement Studio supports complex flows.

sampleQuestions.question: What does the Pardot-Salesforce connector sync?
options: Prospects, leads, contacts, opportunities, and campaign membership
sampleQuestions.explanation: The connector syncs prospects, leads, contacts, opportunities, and campaigns.

sampleQuestions.question: Which best practice applies to form design in Pardot?
options: Use as many fields as possible
Minimize fields, use progressive profiling, and align with lifecycle stages
sampleQuestions.explanation: Fewer fields, progressive profiling, and lifecycle alignment improve conversion.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of dynamic content in Pardot emails?
options: To send the same content to everyone
To personalize content based on prospect attributes or list membership
sampleQuestions.explanation: Dynamic content personalizes emails by audience or attributes.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Pardot report helps measure marketing ROI?
options: Campaign ROI, opportunity influence, and conversion reports
sampleQuestions.explanation: Campaign ROI and opportunity influence reports measure marketing impact.

sampleQuestions.question: What does lifecycle stage represent in Pardot?
options: The prospect's position in the buyer journey (e.g., Subscriber, Lead, MQL)
sampleQuestions.explanation: Lifecycle stage tracks where the prospect is in the buyer journey.

sampleQuestions.question: How should a consultant approach Pardot implementation?
options: Discover requirements, design solution, configure, and train
sampleQuestions.explanation: Implementation should include discovery, design, configuration, and training.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Pardot asset can trigger automation when a prospect views it?
options: Landing pages, forms, and custom redirects (trackable links)
sampleQuestions.explanation: Landing pages, forms, and custom redirects can trigger automation on view.
